Note 2 (ticket 1), written by IT agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: full_time (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write

As a full-time employee, max is write, and admin requires owning the system—Payroll Specialist does not own Source Code (Engineer does). Requested level (write) is at the maximum, so recommend write.
Note 3 (ticket 1), written by Finance agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent, note 2 by IT agent)
  - employment type: full_time (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent, note 2 by IT agent)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Finance DB confirms Edward Fleming (E042) is a Payroll Specialist; team notes indicate full-time. He requested write access to Source Code. As a full-time employee, max is write; admin requires owning the system, and Payroll Specialist does not own Source Code (Engineer does). Requested level (write) is at the maximum, so recommend write.
Note 4 (ticket 1), written by Compliance agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent, note 2 by IT agent, note 3 by Finance agent)
  - employment type: full_time (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent, note 2 by IT agent, note 3 by Finance agent)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Compliance DB confirms Edward Fleming (E042) is a Payroll Specialist; team notes indicate full-time. He requested write access to Source Code. As a full-time employee, max is write; admin requires owning the system, and Payroll Specialist does not own Source Code (Engineer does). Requested level (write) is at the maximum, so recommend write.
Note 5 (ticket 1), written by Facilities agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent, note 2 by IT agent, note 3 by Finance agent, note 4 by Compliance agent)
  - employment type: full_time (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent, note 2 by IT agent, note 3 by Finance agent, note 4 by Compliance agent)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Facilities DB confirms Edward Fleming (E042) is a Payroll Specialist; team notes indicate full-time. He requested write access to Source Code. As a full-time employee, max is write; admin requires owning the system, and Payroll Specialist does not own Source Code (Engineer does). Requested level (write) is at the maximum, so recommend write.
Note 6 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Edward Fleming (E042) is a contractor with basic security training (not full-time as other notes assumed). Contractors max is read unless they have advanced training, which he does not. Requested write exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: Security DB (verified) shows Edward Fleming (E042) is a contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced security training. He does not have advanced training, so the maximum is read. Requested write exceeds the maximum, so grant read.

Note 3 (Finance): not looked up; same as note 1
Note 4 (Compliance): not looked up; same as note 1

Note 6 (Security): employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing); security training: basic (looked up)

Hmm, as the Approver, I need to make a decision. The access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

If full_time: requested write ≤ max write → grant write.
If contractor with basic training: max read → requested write above max → grant read.

- Requested level (write) exceeds his maximum, so I grant the maximum.
